selection_notes: Lowest-cost true 500mA-class 3.3V LDO with deep stock. Runner-ups: AP2112K-3.3TRG1 (C51118, $0.16, 600mA), XC6206P332MR ($0.017 but only 200-250mA, misses the tier).
JLC Basic jellybean with 2.1M stock; Basic avoids the extended-part setup fee at assembly. Cheaper Extended clone: AMS1117-3.3 C347222 ($0.043). Allow >=1.3V dropout headroom.
Diodes Inc 5A-rated LDO, best price with healthy stock in the 3A+ class. Runner-up LM1084S-3.3/TR (C259972, $0.37). Genuine LM1085ISX-3.3 is $2.01. Linear at 3A dissipates hard: budget copper area.
Canonical cheap booster. MT3608L (C2932326, $0.044) is cheaper but a 16V-max-input variant. TPS61023 (C919459, $0.27) when synchronous rectification or low-battery behavior matters.

Only big-switch parts genuinely deliver 2A+ at 5V from 3.0-4.2V in. FP6293 (C83576, $0.53, 3.5A switch) covers ~1.5A budget builds. TPS61021A has 71K stock but tops out at 4.4V output, so it is ineligible.
TI 2A synchronous buck at $0.07 with 189K stock. SY8089A1AAC (C479074, $0.09, 282K stock) is equivalent. ME3116 (C97643, $0.14) when Vin can reach 40V.
Fixed-output wide-Vin buck with minimal externals; the standard pick for 12V/24V inputs down to 3.3V.
Same family as AP63203 (one footprint serves both rails).
Best price/stock 3A buck by a wide margin (152K stock). MP1584EN is $2.91 at LCSC despite its cheap-module reputation. XL4015E1 (C51661, $0.67) when 5A or a dirt-simple 180kHz design is acceptable.
469K stock at $0.07. Original TopPower TP4056-42-ESOP8 is C16581 ($0.19). TP4057 (C725791, $0.039, SOT-23-6, 500mA) for tiny boards; MCP73831 (C424093, $0.81) when a name brand is required.

Everlight, responds across visible and IR. PD15-22B/TR8 (C161211, $0.10) is the IR-only twin. VBPW34S (C145262, $0.59) for large-area needs. PT17-21C ($0.06, 0805) is a phototransistor when gain beats linearity.
Cheaper than the 12-bit ADS1015IDGSR ($1.62) in the same snapshot, so the 16-bit part wins on both price and resolution.

Diodes Inc linear hall, well documented and stocked. OH49E (C49021369, $0.28) is a cheaper clone; SS49E (C85697) is the TO-92S through-hole classic. For a digital switch instead, use an omnipolar SOT-23 part like SLSS49E-3 (C2904393, $0.15).
VL53L0X module-on-chip; the hobby standard. VL53L1CXV0FY/1 (C190004, $4.82) doubles the range to 4m.
Cheapest current-production 3-axis part. Stock was moderate (1.3K) at snapshot; LIS3DHTR (C15134, $1.09, 6.2K stock) is the better-stocked fallback. ADXL345 runs $3.45+.
Standalone gyros are effectively EOL at LCSC (L3GD20 unstocked, A3G4250D stock 18 at snapshot), so this row deliberately points at the 6-axis IMU default.
82K stock at $1.54. QMI8658A (C3021082, $1.62, 54K stock) is a close second. MPU-6050 is EOL and now $14.92 at LCSC; avoid in new designs.
Integrated digital pyro sensor (through-hole). AM312 had no stock at snapshot. BISS0001 (C404323, $0.11) is the analog-controller route when paired with a bare pyro element.
Best price/stock by 2x (55K stock at $0.97). TMC2209-LA-T (C2150710, $2.70) for silent StealthChop and UART config; DRV8825PWPR (C81582, $2.17) for supplies up to 45V.
JLC Basic across common values. Representative 10k 0402WGF1002TCE = C25744 ($0.0013, 7.2M stock at snapshot). Specific values resolve within the series.
JLC Basic across common values. Representative 10k 0603WAF1002T5E = C25804 ($0.0033, 7.6M stock at snapshot).
JLC Basic across common values. Representative 10k 0805W8F1002T5E = C17414 ($0.0030, 14.1M stock at snapshot).
Representative 100nF/25V CL05A104KA5NNNC = C100072 ($0.0024 at snapshot). Mind voltage/capacitance derating at 0402.
JLC Basic for common values. Representative 1uF/50V CL10A105KB8NNNC = C15849 ($0.011, 6.1M stock at snapshot).
Representative 10uF/16V CL21A106KOQNNNE = C1713 ($0.019; that exact value was thin at snapshot, but the series is the LCSC standard for 0805 bulk capacitance).
The Adafruit/SparkFun standard for battery percentage; no cheaper stocked option exists (MAX17043 $7.51 at 256 stock, LC709203 unstocked). Pairs with lipo-charger-1s.
Cheaper, deeper-stocked AND better-specced (36V, 16-bit, alert pin) than the Adafruit-classic INA219 (C87469, $0.84, 20K). INA3221 (C181255, $1.56) for three channels.
The Adafruit breakout favorite because it is a fraction of Sensirion pricing. SHT40-CD1B-R3 (C7461852, $1.89) or SHT30 (~$2.8-3.0) when accuracy specs matter; DHT20 is the same die in SIP-4.

Genuine BMP280 has drifted to $6.87 with 4.5K stock, so the newer BMP388 wins on every axis (29K stock). BME280 ($6.36) adds humidity, but AHT20 + BMP388 together is cheaper. BMP390/BMP581 unstocked at snapshot.
Adafruit's current lux pick and the price winner. BH1750FVI-TR (C78960, $0.93, 36K stock) is the GY-302 classic with deeper stock; OPT3001 (C90462, $1.23) the TI option.

Adafruit's current magnetometer chip and by far the cheapest stocked compass. Mind the tiny 0.8mm WLP (machine assembly only); QMC5883P (C2847467, $1.53, LGA-16 3x3) when a friendlier package is worth 5x the price. With imu-6axis this covers 9-DOF, which is why pricey fusion parts (BNO055 $10) are not defaulted.

The probe-able hobby classic (waterproof probe assemblies everywhere). UMW second source at half the genuine price (DS18B20+ C9753, $1.20). For on-board I2C temperature, TMP102 (C99269, $0.32) or the temp-humidity row.
The jellybean inside every cheap touch module. AT42QT1010 (C74512, $1.31) is the SparkFun/Adafruit name brand; MPR121QR2 (C91322, $2.67) for 12 pads.
For ESP32 voice projects. The breakout classics are gone at LCSC (INMP441 and SPH0645 unstocked); name-brand ICS-43434 is $6.77. MEMSensing MSM261 series is the stocked current standard.

Dual H-bridge: the breakout default for differential-drive robots. TB6612FNG (C88224, $1.13) is the Adafruit-classic equivalent; DRV8837 (C39159, $0.21, 55K stock) when one motor suffices; L9110S ($0.13-0.17) the bargain single.
The Adafruit 16-channel servo-driver classic with no real substitute at LCSC; only needed beyond the MCU's own PWM channels.
I2S mono class-D used across Chinese ESP32 speaker designs; easiest package of the stocked options. MAX98357A is the Adafruit classic (TQFN C910544 $1.28; BGA-9 C2682619 $0.51 but a 1.3mm BGA).
The Adafruit speaker-amp staple, picked over the stereo PAM8403 ($0.17 but thin 2.7K no-brand stock) for stock depth and a known source. Use two for stereo.
NeoPixel, 336K stock. SK6812MINI-E (C5149201, $0.087) for the 3.5mm mini, WS2812B-2020/4020 for tighter boards; chain any count off one data GPIO.

PCF8563-compatible used across M5Stack hardware; deepest stock at the lowest price tier. Genuine NXP PCF8563T (C7440, $0.59); DS3231MZ (C107410, $2.94) when TCXO precision matters (the Adafruit precision-RTC classic); DS1307 is 5V-only legacy.

83K stock, no crystal needed. NOTE: the design skill's flashing prose references CH340N, which had 31 units in stock at snapshot; CH340C is the same family in a stocked package. CH343P (C2846043, $1.25) for 6Mbps; CP2102N ($1.64+) the SiLabs option.
16-bit expander at the lowest verified price. PCF8574 (UMW C22396383, $0.56) is the 8-bit classic; MCP23017 (C558584, $1.68) the Adafruit breakout staple if its register model is preferred.
The Adafruit address-conflict fixer, cheap enough to default. PCA9548APW (C21198, $0.99) is the same function from NXP.
